verdict.rationale: PayPal's ACP/UCP agentic checkout flows do generate scoped, single-use payment tokens — Braintree payment method nonces 'bound to your merchant ID' with configurable 'amount and time restrictions', and Google Pay tokenized single-use credentials — used instead of raw card numbers during agent checkout. This matches the spirit of scoped/limited-use credentials, but the token is generated automatically within the checkout protocol (by ChatGPT/Google/merchant), not something the end-user proactively mints or configures per-agent, and merchant-restriction scoping is set by the merchant/protocol rather than the user. Missing for 10: user-facing credential creation/configuration flow, user-controlled merchant-restriction settings, and independent/hands-on confirmation of these restrictions working end-to-end.
